questions.feedback: That trap answer is the one to unlearn: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km. Reteach point: Speed is distance per hour: after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, not 60.

questions.prompt: A bus travels at 60 km/h for half an hour. How far has it travelled?

questions.answer: 150 km: distance = speed × time, so 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.
questions.feedback: Scene s2 locks the method: multiply speed by time - 60 km in each full hour plus 30 km in the half hour gives 150 km in 2.5 hours.
questions.prompt: Work out how far a bus travelling at 60 km/h goes in 2.5 hours, showing the working.

questions.feedback: Scene s4 fixes the formula: distance = speed × time, so at 50 km/h for 3 hours the distance is 50 × 3 = 150 km.
questions.prompt: Which working finds the distance travelled at 50 km/h for 3 hours?

questions.answer: 60 km/h: speed = distance ÷ time, so 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.
